subject: problems with fitted errors in space time models

messages.author: 833479854a80815e
messages.subject: problems with fitted errors in space time models
parts:
Dear all,

I am kindly asking for your help.:)

My problem setup is the following:  I have 56 measurement stations for rain over 12 month and I look at the aggregated monthly values (total of 672 space time data), so I built the observation matrix and my index as:

A.est<-inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc=coords,group=monthly.value$Time,n.group = month)
and
index<-inla.spde.make.index("field", n.spde=spde$n.spde, n.group=month)

I know that rain is in general gamma distributed, but I transform it via log(rain) to a gauss distribution. 

My formula is then:
formula<-log(rain)~-1+Intercept+f(field,model=spde,group=field.group, control.group = list(model="ar1"))
And I perform INLA (where my stack consists of observation data; no prediction stack so far).

Then I project my spatial field to a grid and get a projection of the random field for every time step by 
inla.mesh.project( projgrid, result$summary.random$field$mean[index$field.group == j])
(Please correct me but this is not on the log-scale as I only transformed my response to log-scale right? :) )

Then I continue to get the expected precipitation: I get 14272 pred.points within my area of interest, build a prediction stack, combine it with the estimation stack, and run INLA again. But now, I am struggeling to plot my expected rain  for each of my 12 month. Do you have any idea if I can fix this problem?
 
And now I need to back transform from the log-scale for sure but for the standard deviation it is not just the exponent(sd) right?

I am so much looking forward to your help.

All the best,
Corinna

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] problems with fitted errors in space time models
parts:
Hi,

If you have included all the terms in the prediction stack, you can take the summary.fitted.values and use it considering that it is the summary of the posterior marginal distributions for E(log(y)) at each one of the 14272 points (use the inla.stack.index() function to get the right 14272 elements).

The sd column in the summary.fitted.values is the standard error of the expected value of the logarithm of y, SD(E(log(y))), and is not not SD(log(y)). To have SD(log(y)) you need to account for the precision of the likelihood, or the error after the linear predictor.

The easiest way to have SD(y) is considering Monte Carlo samples from the joint posterior. Then use these samples to have samples from y at each prediction point. This is easier if you consider inlabru this is a lot easier, as you can see from this tutorial https://inlabru-org.github.io/inlabru/articles/web/random_fields_2d.html

best regards,
Elias

messages.author: 833479854a80815e
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] problems with fitted errors in space time models
parts:
Dear Elias,

thank you so much for your response. 

Still I have one more question: I include the spatially and temporally structured random effect via the group function in the f() term of my formula. 
I project the mean of my random field to a fine grid by 
xmean <- list()
for (j in 1:month){
  xmean[[j]] <- inla.mesh.project( projgrid, result$summary.random$field$mean[index$field.group == j])
  xmean[[j]][!xy.in] <- NA
}

But now I am also looking for a projection of my fitted values related to each month j (12 in total). How do I get these values?

I only manage to get result2$summary.fitted.values[index.pred,"mean"] which gives me one plot instead of 12. 

Again thanks for your time in advance. 

All the best,
Corinna
